title: Suturing a flap laceration
stem: Procedure room. Mr Chan, 58, a construction worker, has a V-shaped flap laceration on his left shin from a metal edge 3 hours ago. Take a brief history, get his consent, and repair it on the skin model.

phases.title: History and consent
phases.goal: Brief history (mechanism, tetanus, allergies, healing risks) and informed consent.

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: The right kit and the right suture.

phases.title: Repair
phases.goal: By hand: anaesthetise, clean out, anchor the tip, then close it stitch by stitch.

phases.title: Aftercare
phases.goal: Tetanus, suture removal, and warning signs.

review.text: Lidocaine maximum. Your notes use 4 mg/kg, the US figure. UK practice: 3 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with adrenaline.

Tetanus. A booster is not decided only by '>10 years since the last dose'. UKHSA: a tetanus-prone wound (soil, manure, over 6 hours, devitalised tissue) needs a booster if the patient is not fully immunised, and immunoglobulin too if the wound is high-risk.

notes:
Checked against RCEM/BSSH wound care principles, the UKHSA Green Book tetanus chapter (2023 update), and standard suturing technique.

Assess: mechanism, time, contamination, foreign body, tendon/nerve/vessel injury, tetanus status, diabetes/peripheral vascular disease (pretibial wounds in older patients heal poorly — consider steri-strips for thin skin). Prepare: aseptic field, irrigation with saline, local anaesthetic (1% lidocaine, max 3 mg/kg plain or 7 mg/kg with adrenaline; your notes use 4 mg/kg, the US figure), explore, debride non-viable tissue. Flap: the half-buried horizontal mattress (corner) stitch at the tip preserves blood supply; simple interrupted sutures elsewhere (vertical mattress where eversion is needed). 4-0 non-absorbable monofilament on the leg; removal at 10–14 days for the lower leg (7–10 days for other limb sites). Non-adherent dressing. Tetanus: a tetanus-prone wound (soil, manure, delay over 6 hours, devitalised tissue) needs a booster if not fully immunised or last dose over 10 years ago, and immunoglobulin for high-risk wounds in someone not fully immunised (UKHSA) — not simply '>10 years since last dose'.

Your notes cover the procedure, handling of sharps and instruments, and complications, matching this.

Perfect script checked against the RCEM wound guidance and UKHSA tetanus guidance, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. The flow you reviewed is kept; the silk option and the bench's pick-up-with-fingers button are removed. Surgical gym complete.

steps.label: Talk to Mr Chan
steps.hint: Introduce, explain and consent; how and when, contamination; tetanus; allergies; diabetes, circulation, steroids, blood thinners.

opts.t: Hello Mr Chan, I'm the emergency doctor. I'd like to clean the wound, numb it and stitch it. It may hurt a little, and there's a small risk of infection and a scar. Do I have your consent to go ahead?
opts.tz: 陳生你好，我係急症室醫生。我會幫你清洗傷口、打麻醉，再縫埋佢；可能會有啲痛、有機會發炎同留疤。你同意嗎？
opts.mark: Introduces, explains the procedure and risks, obtains consent

opts.t: How did it happen, exactly when, and was it dirty? Any glass or metal in it?
opts.tz: 點樣整親㗎？幾點鐘嘅事？傷口污唔污糟？有冇玻璃或者金屬入咗去？
opts.r: A sheet of metal on site caught my shin about three hours ago. It was dusty there.
opts.rz: 喺地盤俾塊鐵皮界親，大概三個鐘頭前。嗰度好多塵。

opts.t: When was your last tetanus injection?
opts.tz: 你上一次打破傷風針係幾時？

opts.t: Any allergies: to local anaesthetic, antiseptic, plasters or any medicine?
opts.tz: 你對麻醉藥、消毒藥水、膠布或者任何藥物有冇敏感？

opts.t: Any diabetes, poor circulation, steroids or blood thinners? Do you smoke?
opts.tz: 你有冇糖尿病、血液循環唔好、食緊類固醇或者薄血藥？有冇食煙？
opts.r: None of those. I smoke a few a day.
opts.mark: Healing risks: diabetes, vascular disease, steroids, anticoagulants

opts.t: Thank you. I'll start the repair now
opts.tz: 多謝你，我而家開始幫你處理傷口。
opts.early: You haven't asked whether I'm happy for you to go ahead.

steps.label: Prepare
steps.hint: Suture set, sterile gloves and drape, antiseptic, saline, lidocaine, 4-0 nylon, dressing, sharps bin.

opts.t: Suture pack, sterile gloves, drape, chlorhexidine
Normal saline and syringe for irrigation
Non-adherent dressing; sharps bin at hand

steps.label: Repair the flap
steps.hint: Flap tip and foot, infiltrate through the edges (needle to the bin), test, irrigate, lift and explore under the flap, corner stitch, interrupted sutures, sharps, dressing.

opts.performHint: Do it with your hands. Every bite is judged as you place it.
mark: Neurovascular status: flap tip refill, foot pulses and sensation
Local infiltration through the wound edges
Places a corner stitch at the flap tip

steps.label: Aftercare
steps.hint: Tetanus, suture removal time, wound care, infection signs.

opts.t: Your last tetanus was 15 years ago and the wound was dirty, so a booster today.
opts.tz: 你上次打破傷風針係十五年前，個傷口又污糟，所以今日要打多支加強針。

opts.t: The stitches come out in 10 to 14 days on the lower leg. Keep it dry for 48 hours and keep the leg raised.
opts.tz: 小腿嘅線要十至十四日先拆；頭兩日唔好整濕；隻腳要墊高。
opts.mark: Suture removal timing and wound care

opts.t: Come back if it gets red, oozes pus, you get a fever, or the pain increases.
opts.tz: 如果傷口紅腫、有膿、發燒，或者越嚟越痛，就要返嚟。

qs.a: Anchors the tip without strangling it
wrong: Faster closure of the whole wound
Better cosmesis, but only on the face and neck
A surgical incision closed within 6 hours

qs.q: Vertical mattress suture is useful for…
wrong: Inverting the edges of the wound

badge.name: Stitch Master
badge.flavor: Irrigate, explore, corner stitch the tip, everted edges, never touch the needle.

options: Less infection risk and tissue drag
Any wound more than 10 years after the last dose
Through intact skin 5 cm away only
After suturing, into the closed wound

cards.q: Pretibial flap in an elderly patient with thin skin?
options: Leave open to heal by secondary intention

script.say: Hello Mr Chan, I'm the emergency doctor. I'd like to clean the wound, numb it and stitch it. It may hurt a little, and there's a small risk of infection and a scar. Do I have your consent to go ahead? How did it happen, exactly when, and was it dirty? Any glass or metal in it? When was your last tetanus injection?
script.do: Yes, go ahead, doctor. A sheet of metal on site caught my shin about three hours ago. It was dusty there. About 15 years ago, I think.

script.say: Any allergies: to local anaesthetic, antiseptic, plasters or any medicine? Any diabetes, poor circulation, steroids or blood thinners? Do you smoke? Thank you. I'll start the repair now.
script.do: No allergies. None of those. I smoke a few a day. Okay, doctor.

script.say: Suture pack, sterile gloves, drape, chlorhexidine. Normal saline and syringe for irrigation. 1% lidocaine, 10 mL syringe, orange needle.
4-0 non-absorbable monofilament (nylon). Non-adherent dressing; sharps bin at hand.

Check the flap tip refill, foot pulses and sensation first. 1% lidocaine through the wound edges, under 3 mg per kg; needle straight to the sharps bin. Test it's numb, irrigate with saline, lift the flap and explore for foreign bodies, trim dead tissue. Needle in the needle holder. A corner stitch at the flap tip: skin, through the tip, skin. Then simple interrupted stitches, square to the edge, equal bites on each side, evenly spaced. Sharps to the bin, non-adherent dressing.

Your last tetanus was 15 years ago and the wound was dirty, so a booster today. The stitches come out in 10 to 14 days on the lower leg. Keep it dry for 48 hours and keep the leg raised. Come back if it gets red, oozes pus, you get a fever, or the pain increases.
